Day 2 Convective Outlook  
NWS Storm Prediction Center Norman OK
1239 AM CDT Thu Aug 06 2026

Valid 071200Z - 081200Z

...THERE IS A MARGINAL RISK OF SEVERE THUNDERSTORMS OVER PARTS OF
THE UPPER MISSISSIPPI VALLEY REGION...AND PARTS OF THE NORTHEAST...

...SUMMARY...
A few strong to severe storms may occur from Iowa across Wisconsin
and into Upper Michigan Friday, with areas of strong/damaging wind
gusts and isolated marginal hail. Other storms may produce locally
damaging gusts over parts of the Northeast.

...IA...southeast MN...WI...Upper MI...
Moderate northwest flow aloft will move across the northern Plains
and into the Upper MS Valley, with a cold front extending from
northwest WI into IA by late afternoon. A moist air mass with 70s F
dewpoints will exist ahead of the front, contributing to 2000-3000
J/kg MUCAPE. Supporting the potentially strong instability will be
relatively cool 500 mb temperatures to around -10 C.

Storms are likely to form during the afternoon along the front with
scattered marginal hail or strong wind gusts. Deep-layer shear will
not be particularly strong. Some potential may develop for an MCS
over southern areas including IA, and this area will be monitored
for potential greater wind probabilities.

...Northern VA into PA and southern NY...
Midlevel southwesterlies around 25 kt will exist across the
northeastern states on Friday, with weak height falls occurring as a
primary upper trough moves across the Great Lake region. In the low
levels, west/southwest winds around the Atlantic high will maintain
a warm/moist air mass, which when heated during the afternoon should
yield up to 2000 J/kg MUCAPE, especially near the coastal areas
where dewpoints will be higher.

Despite lack of any surface boundaries, model consensus is for
scattered storms to develop from northern VA/MD into central to
eastern PA and across southern NY during the afternoon. Shear will
be weak but a few clusters of storms may produce gusty winds.

..Jewell.. 08/06/2026

Day 3 Convective Outlook  
NWS Storm Prediction Center Norman OK
0211 AM CDT Thu Aug 06 2026

Valid 081200Z - 091200Z

...THERE IS A MARGINAL RISK OF SEVERE THUNDERSTORMS FROM NEBRASKA
INTO PARTS OF IOWA AND NORTHERN MISSOURI...

...SUMMARY...
A corridor of damaging winds may develop Saturday afternoon and
evening from Nebraska into Iowa/Northern Missouri.

...Mid to Lower MO Valley...
Moderate northwest flow aloft will persist across the northern
Plains into the Great Lakes on Saturday, as the main upper wave
rotates northeast from Ontario into Quebec. The southern periphery
of this stronger flow aloft will remain over the middle to lower MO
Valley, with a warm front developing across NE and IA. Strong
heating will occur east of a surface low either in western NE or KS,
with south winds resulting in a deep mixed layer by afternoon.

Storms are expected to form over NE, and possibly move into IA or MO
through evening in the form of an MCS. This would be fueled by a
strengthening southerly low-level jet as well, suggesting an
organized system may occur. For now, low probabilities have been
added due to uncertainty with placement of any such corridor.
Damaging winds would be the main concern.

...Mid Atlantic...
Scattered afternoon storms will again be likely over much of the
eastern states on Saturday, within a modest southwest flow regime. A
high PW environment will remain in place, supporting an uncapped air
mass and conditional/localized wind risk. Predictability is low at
this time given possible antecedent rain or thunderstorm areas, but
low probabilities for wind could be added in later updates.

..Jewell.. 08/06/2026

Day 4-8 Convective Outlook  
NWS Storm Prediction Center Norman OK
0300 AM CDT Thu Aug 06 2026

Valid 091200Z - 141200Z

...DISCUSSION...
For the Sunday/D4 through Thursday/D8 period, an elongated zone of
thunderstorm/wind potential will exist from the northern Plains
across parts of the Midwest/Great Lakes, and possibly extending into
parts of the Northeast. Predictability is low for this pattern given
the likelihood of ongoing corridors of storms early each day, and
variability with the position of the elongated west to east front.
However, the presence of a very moist air mass, with possibly strong
instability to the south, combined with possible waves rotating
around the large-scale upper trough over Canada, may yield storm
corridors with damaging wind potential. One or more areas may be
denoted in later outlooks as the events near in time.

At this time, rough areas of interest include the northern Plains to
Upper Midwest on Sunday/D4, and portions of the Great Lakes/Midwest
on Monday/D5.

..Jewell.. 08/06/2026

Day 1 Convective Outlook CORR 1
NWS Storm Prediction Center Norman OK
0826 AM CDT Thu Aug 06 2026

Valid 061300Z - 071200Z

...THERE IS A SLIGHT RISK OF SEVERE THUNDERSTORMS FOR NORTHEAST
OKLAHOMA AND SOUTHEAST KANSAS INTO THE MISSOURI OZARKS...

CORRECTED FOR WIND LINES

...SUMMARY...
Isolated to widely scattered severe thunderstorms capable primarily
of a severe-wind threat will be possible this afternoon and evening
over parts of Ozarks and Great Plains.  Isolated strong to locally
severe gusts capable of wind damage are possible from the
Mid-Atlantic northward into New York.

...Ozarks westward into the southern High Plains...
Water-vapor imagery shows a mid-level anticyclone centered over
AZ/UT and a broad trough over the Upper Midwest favoring modest
west-northwesterly mid to high-level flow across the central Plains.
Several clusters of showers/thunderstorms are ongoing this morning
from the mid MS Valley and lower MO Valley into the OK-KS border
region.  Much of this activity is located to the north of a residual
front and outflow draped from the TX Panhandle east-northeast into
the mid MS Valley.  South of the boundary, an appreciably moist
airmass, featuring 50s F dewpoints west to lower 70s east, will heat
in areas void of convection and related cloud debris.  It is
uncertain how much influence morning showers/storms will have across
the Slight Risk area.  Nonetheless, model forecast soundings show
moderate destabilization occurring by mid-late afternoon across much
of this region.  Isolated to widely scattered storms will
preferentially develop near the effective front/outflow.  Some storm
organization is possible with the main threat being isolated to
widely scattered severe gusts.  Have adjusted the level 1 intensity
for wind to northern OK westward into the southern High Plains where
steep low-level lapse rates are forecast.  A couple of multicell
clusters may eventually evolve during the early evening.  A relative
minimum in storm activity may occur over parts of the TX Panhandle
in between storms over the northeast NM/western part of the TX
Panhandle and higher coverage of storms farther east over northern
OK into the Ozarks.  

...Mid-Atlantic into the Northeast...
Mid-level flow will be southwesterly over the Northeast today.  At
the surface, a trough will be located from the Atlantic Coastal
Plains of Virginia north-northeastward into the southeastern New
York.  As surface temperatures warm today, thunderstorms will
develop in the foothills of the Appalachians, moving
east-northeastward into the lower elevations and toward the surface
trough.  Surface dewpoints near the trough will be in the lower to
mid 70s F, which will contribute to moderate destabilization by
early afternoon (MLCAPE 1000-2500 J/kg).  Some of the stronger
water-loaded downdrafts will be capable of an isolated risk for wind
damage.  

...Western Nebraska/southern South Dakota...
West-northwesterly mid-level flow will be in place over much of the
north-central U.S.  At the surface, an axis of low-level
moisture will set up from western Nebraska into far southern South
Dakota, where dewpoints will be in the 60s F.  Near this axis, model
forecasts show a pocket of moderate instability this afternoon with
MLCAPE around 2000 J/kg.  Although large-scale ascent will be weak,
any cell that can initiate near the instability axis could be
capable of producing isolated severe gusts/large hail.

..Smith/Bentley.. 08/06/2026
